title: New Zealand Name Conway and Ravindra for India Tests, Subject to Fitness
excerpt: Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell are all in New Zealand's 14-player squad for the two Tests against India but must prove their fitness before the Wellington opener on November 19.
body:
• New Zealand have named a 14-player Test squad for the two-match series against India, captained by Tom Latham, with the first Test starting at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 19.
  • Devon Conway (concussion), Rachin Ravindra (dislocated shoulder) and Tom Blundell (quadricep) are all included but are aiming to be fit for the first Test — none is yet confirmed available.
  • Pacer Jacob Duffy returns; Ben Sears (ankle), Zak Foulkes (hip) and Will O'Rourke (return-to-play programme) miss out.
  • The second Test is at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from November 27, with World Test Championship points on the line.

New Zealand have named Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell in their squad for the two-Test series against India, with all three working to be fit for the first Test in Wellington on November 19, according to the ICC's report of the announcement by New Zealand Cricket.

Tom Latham captains the 14-player squad: Tom Latham (captain), Tom Blundell (wicketkeeper), Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Mitchell Santner, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner and Will Young, according to Cricbuzz.

Three fitness races

Each of the three returning players has a different problem. Conway sustained a concussion in a collision with paceman Matt Henry in training during the one-day series against India, Flashscore reported. Ravindra dislocated his right shoulder while filming a diving catch during a promotional shoot in September and has not played in either the ODI or Twenty20 series against India. Blundell is recovering from a quadricep injury and has played just one domestic match since June. Their inclusion is a selection, not a clearance — availability for Wellington will depend on their recoveries this week.

"The squad is largely consistent with the team that competed in England earlier this year, so it'll be great to be back together to try and recreate some of that success on home soil."

— Rob Walter, New Zealand head coach

Who misses out

From the squad that won 2-1 in England earlier this year, Ben Sears (ankle injury), Zak Foulkes (hip injury) and Will O'Rourke (return-to-play programme) miss out, Cricbuzz reported, along with Kane Williamson, who retired during that series. Jacob Duffy returns to the pace group alongside Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Nathan Smith and Blair Tickner. The series also begins the tenure of newly appointed batting coach BJ Watling, who starts on November 16, according to Cricbuzz.

What is at stake

Head coach Rob Walter framed the series as the start of a busy home summer. "This series marks the start of an exciting summer of Test cricket for the Black Caps," he said. "There are 10 Tests scheduled between now and March, so there's no shortage of action for red-ball fans. Valuable Championship points are on the line of course, but our focus remains on playing our best cricket against a high-quality team like India." Cricbuzz reported that New Zealand currently sit at the top of the World Test Championship standings, and that after India they play a four-match series against Australia in December-January and two Tests against Sri Lanka in February.

Fixtures

The first Test starts at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 19. The second Test is at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from November 27, according to Flashscore. For diaspora fans, the open question before Wellington is the fitness one: whether Conway, Ravindra and Blundell are cleared in time will shape New Zealand's top order and wicketkeeping choice for the series opener.
